text.p: - Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-An international study shows European managers regard Oslo as one of the least attractive cities for setting up business. On a list of 30 European cities, Oslo ranks number 27. The list is topped by London while Athens is last. But managers think the air is cleaner in Oslo than in other places.
- So far this year Norwegian customs have confiscated 50 kilos of heroin, nearly 10 kilos more than in 1995.

-Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and its parent, Deutsche Bank, will not be obliged to bid for Norwegian software company Sysdeco Group by the Oslo Stock Exchange. After the irregularities in the MGAM funds came to light in September, MGAM found they owned 51.2 percent of Sysdeco but have since cut their holdings to 47 percent. The bourse ruled the two holdings will be counted separately.
-A member of the parliament's industry committee says the Norwegian state should grant American Atmel billions in support in order to make Atmel locate their microchips production to Norway.
-A strong Norwegian crown causes problems for the Norwegian tourist industry. Prices for tours to Norway in the important German market could increase as much as 10 percent before next season.

-Kvaerner's manager Erik Tonseth announced the nine-month results in London yesterday but he could also be seen in Oslo because the press conference at the group's London headquarters was shown on a video in the Norwegian capital.
